title: A library lending service, from a written note and a later interview that contradicts it
provenance: Synthetic system authored for this corpus (issue #64). Not derived from, or sanitized from, any real system or any real conversation: there is nothing to leak by omission. The transcript's form follows the properties measured from real exports in #51: attribution by participant name, no uncertainty markers, cleaned turns. Its content is invented.
notes: The corpus's first transcript and first two-source case, written for issue #64 to grade the conversational rules and the two-source disagreement rule in prompts/extract.md. Five traps, each recorded as a correction. A hedge on the app's authentication must stay unknown, and the spoofing must-find rests on that unknown. A fact inside a question must produce no kiosk-to-database flow. A self-correction must produce no second database, and a hypothetical must produce no partner entity; both are element-level. The note and the transcript disagree on the lending API's exposure, which must become unknown with both claims in notes, and the elevation-of-privilege must-find rests on it. The domain is a public library, which no other case covers; it has no payment data, and it keeps clear of case 14's loyalty platform, a holdout case.
